questions.question: Which of the following can an AWS customer use to launch a new Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) cluster? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: You can launch an Amazon RDS cluster with AWS CloudFormation (B) (infrastructure as code) and the AWS Management Console (E). Concierge is support, S3 is storage, and EC2 Auto Scaling does not create RDS.

questions.question: Which of the following Reserved Instance (RI) pricing models provides the highest average savings compared to On-Demand pricing?

options.text: One-year, No Upfront, Standard RI pricing.
One-year, All Upfront, Convertible RI pricing.
Three-year, All Upfront, Standard RI pricing.
Three-year, No Upfront, Convertible RI pricing.

questions.explanation: A three-year, All Upfront, Standard RI provides the highest average savings versus On-Demand — longer term, full prepayment, and Standard (vs Convertible) all increase the discount.

questions.question: Which of the following are features of Amazon CloudWatch Logs? (Select TWO)

options.text: Summaries by Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).

questions.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch Logs offers real-time monitoring (D) and adjustable log retention (E). It is not free, does not provide SNS summaries, and does not include free Elasticsearch analytics.

questions.question: Which of the following is an AWS-managed compute service?
questions.explanation: AWS Lambda is an AWS-managed (serverless) compute service. EC2 requires managing instances, SWF orchestrates workflows, and Aurora is a database.

questions.question: A company wants to reduce the physical compute footprint that developers use to run code. Which service would meet that need by enabling serverless architectures?
questions.explanation: AWS Lambda enables serverless architectures, removing the physical compute footprint developers must manage. EC2 requires servers, DynamoDB is a database, and CodeCommit is source control.

questions.question: Which of the following is the customer’s responsibility under the AWS shared responsibility model?
questions.explanation: Patching Amazon EC2 instances (the guest OS and applications) is the customer's responsibility. Patching the underlying infrastructure, physical security, and network infrastructure are AWS responsibilities.

questions.question: According to the AWS shared responsibility model who is responsible for configuration management?

options.text: It is solely the responsibility of the customer.
It is solely the responsibility of AWS.
It is shared between AWS and the customer.
It is not part of the AWS shared responsibility model.

questions.explanation: Configuration management is a shared responsibility: AWS configures its infrastructure devices while customers configure their own guest OS, databases, and applications.

questions.question: Which security service automatically recognizes and classifies sensitive data or intellectual property on AWS?
questions.explanation: Amazon Macie automatically discovers and classifies sensitive data (e.g., PII) in AWS, particularly in S3. GuardDuty detects threats, Inspector assesses vulnerabilities, and Shield mitigates DDoS.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describe the AWS pricing model? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: The AWS pricing model is best described as pay-as-you-go (B) with variable cost (E) — you pay only for what you use. Fixed-term, colocation, and 'planned' do not describe it.

questions.question: Under the shared responsibility model, which of the following tasks are the responsibility of the AWS customer? (Select TWO)

options.text: Ensuring that application data is encrypted at rest.
Ensuring that AWS NTP servers are set to the correct time.
Ensuring that users have received security training in the use of AWS services.
Ensuring that access to data centers is restricted.
Ensuring that hardware is disposed of properly.

questions.explanation: Customers are responsible for encrypting application data at rest (A) and ensuring their users receive security training in using AWS services (C). NTP servers, data-center access, and hardware disposal are AWS responsibilities.

questions.question: A customer is using multiple AWS accounts with separate billing. How can the customer take advantage of volume discounts with minimal impact to the AWS resources?

options.text: Create one global AWS account and move all AWS resources to that account.
Sign up for three years of Reserved Instance pricing up front.
Use the consolidated billing feature from AWS Organizations.
Sign up for the AWS Enterprise support plan to get volume discounts.

questions.explanation: Using consolidated billing through AWS Organizations lets the customer combine usage for volume discounts with minimal change to existing resources. Merging accounts, prepaying RIs, or buying Enterprise Support are not the right approach.

questions.question: Which Amazon EC2 pricing model offers the MOST significant discount when compared to OnDemand Instances?

options.text: A Partial Upfront Reserved Instances for a 1-year term.
All Upfront Reserved instances for a 1 year form.
All Upfront Reserved Instances for a 3 year term.
No Upfront Reserved Instances for a 3 year term.

questions.explanation: All Upfront Reserved Instances for a 3-year term offer the most significant discount versus On-Demand among the options. Shorter terms and partial/no upfront payments discount less.

questions.question: Which AWS services should be used for read/write of constantly changing data? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: For constantly changing read/write data, Amazon RDS (B) (relational) and Amazon EFS (E) (file system) are appropriate. Glacier and Snowball are for archival/transfer, and Redshift is a read-heavy data warehouse.

questions.question: Which AWS service allows users to identify the changes made to a resource over time?
questions.explanation: AWS Config records and tracks changes to a resource's configuration over time. Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, Service Catalog governs products, and IAM manages access.

questions.question: According to best practices, how should an application be designed to run in the AWS Cloud?
questions.explanation: Applications should be designed with loosely coupled components so failures and changes in one do not cascade to others. Tight/'infrequent'/'frequent' coupling are not the best practice.

questions.question: Which benefits are included with the AWS Business Support plan? (Select TWO)

options.text: 24/7 assistance by way of live chat or a telephone call.
Support from a dedicated AWS Technical Account Manager.
An unlimited number of cases and contacts.
15-minute response time for production system interruption cases.
Annual operational reviews with AWS Solutions Architects.

questions.explanation: Business Support provides 24/7 phone/chat/email access (A) and an unlimited number of cases and contacts (C). A dedicated TAM, 15-minute critical response, and operational reviews are Enterprise features.

questions.question: Which of the following is an AWS managed Domain Name System (DNS) web service?
questions.explanation: Amazon Route 53 is AWS's managed DNS web service. Neptune is a graph DB, SageMaker is ML, and Lightsail is simplified hosting.

questions.question: A user must meet compliance and software licensing requirements that state a workload must be hosted on a physical server. When Amazon EC2 instance pricing option will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 Dedicated Hosts provide a physical server dedicated to you, meeting compliance and server-bound software licensing requirements. Dedicated Instances isolate hardware but expose less host detail; Spot/Reserved are pricing models.

questions.question: Which of the Reserved Instance (RI) pricing models can change the attributes of the RI as long as the exchange results in the creation of RIs of equal or greater value?
questions.explanation: Convertible Reserved Instances let you change RI attributes as long as the exchange results in RIs of equal or greater value. Standard RIs cannot change family/attributes the same way.

questions.question: Which service is best for storing common database query results, which helps to alleviate database access load?
questions.explanation: Amazon ElastiCache caches common database query results in memory, reducing load on the database. Amazon ML, SQS, and instance store do not serve as a query cache.

questions.question: When should a company consider using Amazon EC2 Spot Instances? (Select TWO)

options.text: For applications that cannot have interruptions.

questions.explanation: Spot Instances suit non-production applications (A) and fault-tolerant, flexible workloads (D) that can handle interruption. They are not for stateful, uninterruptible, or sensitive database workloads.

questions.question: Which AWS tools assist with estimating costs? (Select three)

options.text: AWS Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) Calculator.

questions.explanation: Tools that assist with cost estimation include Cost allocation tags (B), the AWS Simple Monthly Calculator (C), and the TCO Calculator (D). Detailed billing reports show actual costs, and 'Cost Estimator' is not a real tool. (Note: the Simple Monthly Calculator and TCO Calculator have since been replaced by the AWS Pricing Calculator.)

questions.question: A company wants to focus on business activities instead of managing compute and capacity. Which AWS service can be used to automatically add or remove Amazon EC2 instances based on demand?
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling automatically adds or removes instances based on demand, freeing the company from manual capacity management. ELB distributes traffic, Route 53 is DNS, and CloudFront is a CDN.

questions.question: Which is the minimum AWS Support plan that includes Infrastructure Event Management without additional costs?
questions.explanation: Infrastructure Event Management is included at no extra cost only with the Enterprise Support plan (it is available for an additional fee with Business). Lower tiers do not include it.

questions.question: Access keys in AWS Identity and Access Management (IM1) are used to:

options.text: Log in to the AWS Management Console.
Make programmatic calls to AWS from AWS APIs.
Log in to Amazon EC2 instances.

questions.explanation: IAM access keys are used to make programmatic calls to AWS via the API, CLI, and SDKs. Console sign-in uses a username/password, and instance login uses key pairs.

questions.question: Which AWS service can be used to query stored datasets directly from Amazon S3 using standard SQL?
questions.explanation: Amazon Athena lets you query datasets directly in Amazon S3 using standard SQL, with no servers to manage. Glue is ETL, Data Pipeline orchestrates, and CloudSearch is search.

questions.question: How does AWS shorten the time to provision IT resources?

options.text: It supplies an online IT ticketing platform for resource requests.
It supports automatic code validation services.
It provides the ability to programmatically provision existing resources.
It automates the resource request process from a company’s IT vendor list.

questions.explanation: AWS shortens provisioning time by letting you programmatically provision resources (e.g., via API/CLI/CloudFormation) in minutes. IT ticketing, code validation, and vendor automation are not how AWS speeds provisioning.

questions.question: Which AWS services can be used to gather information about AWS account activity? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail (C) records API/account activity and Amazon CloudWatch (E) collects metrics and logs; both gather information about account activity. CloudFront, Cloud9, and CloudHSM do not.

questions.question: Which of the following are characteristics of Amazon S3? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 is an object store (B) and a highly durable storage system (E) (11 nines). It is not a global/local/network file system.

questions.question: A user wants guidance on possible savings when migrating from on-premises to AWS. Which tool is suitable for this scenario?

options.text: AWS Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) Calculator.

questions.explanation: The AWS TCO Calculator gives guidance on potential savings when migrating from on-premises to AWS. (Note: it has since been folded into the AWS Pricing Calculator.) Budgets, Cost Explorer, and the Well-Architected Tool serve other purposes.

questions.question: Which of the following services is in the category of AWS serverless platform?
questions.explanation: AWS Lambda is part of the AWS serverless platform. EMR, ELB, and Mobile Hub are not serverless compute in this sense.

questions.question: The use of what AWS feature or service allows companies to track and categorize spending on a detailed level?
questions.explanation: Cost allocation tags let companies track and categorize spending at a detailed level (by project, team, environment, etc.). Consolidated billing, Budgets, and Marketplace do not provide this categorization.

questions.question: Which of the following inspects AWS environments to find opportunities that can save money for users and also improve system performance?
questions.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor inspects your environment for opportunities to save money and improve performance (plus security, fault tolerance, and limits). Cost Explorer analyzes spend, and consolidated/detailed billing do not give recommendations.

questions.question: Web servers running on Amazon EC2 access a legacy application running in a corporate data center. What term would describe this model?
questions.explanation: EC2 web servers accessing a legacy application in a corporate data center is a hybrid architecture (cloud plus on-premises). It is not cloud-native, a partner network, or simply IaaS.

questions.question: What technology enables compute capacity to adjust as loads change?
questions.explanation: Auto Scaling adjusts compute capacity automatically as loads change. Load balancing distributes traffic, automatic failover handles outages, and round robin is a routing method.

questions.question: Which AWS service is a managed NoSQL database?
questions.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB is AWS's managed NoSQL database. Redshift is a data warehouse, and Aurora/RDS are relational.

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct relationship between regions, Availability Zones, and edge locations?
questions.explanation: The correct relationship is that Regions contain Availability Zones. Edge locations are separate, and the other orderings are reversed.

questions.question: What approach to transcoding a large number of individual video files adheres to AWS architecture principles?

options.text: Using a single large instance during off-peak hours.
Using a large GPU instance type.

questions.explanation: Transcoding many individual video files adheres to AWS principles by using many instances in parallel (horizontal scaling/parallelization). A single large instance, dedicated hardware, or one big GPU instance does not parallelize the work as well.

questions.question: Which AWS services can host a Microsoft SQL Server database? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: Microsoft SQL Server can run on Amazon EC2 (A) (self-managed) or Amazon RDS (B) (managed). Aurora and Redshift are different engines, and S3 is object storage.

questions.question: Which AWS IAM feature allows developers to access AWS services through the AWS CLI?
questions.explanation: IAM access keys let developers access AWS services through the AWS CLI (and SDKs/API). API keys, console passwords, and SSH keys are for other purposes.

questions.question: The user is fully responsible for which action when running workloads on AWS?

options.text: Implementing controls to route application traffic.

questions.explanation: The customer is fully responsible for implementing controls to route their application traffic (e.g., security groups, routing). Patching/maintaining the underlying infrastructure and physical/environmental controls are AWS's job.

questions.question: Which AWS support plan includes a dedicated Technical Account Manager?
questions.explanation: The Enterprise Support plan includes a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM). Developer, Business, and Basic do not.

questions.question: What time-savings advantage is offered with the use of Amazon Rekognition?

options.text: Amazon Rekognition provides automatic watermarking of images.
Amazon Rekognition provides automatic detection of objects appearing in pictures.
Amazon Recognition provides the ability to resize millions of images automatically.
Amazon Rekognition uses Amazon Mechanical Turk to allow humans to bid on object detection jobs.

questions.explanation: Amazon Rekognition saves time by automatically detecting objects (and scenes, faces, text) in images. It does not watermark, bulk-resize images, or use Mechanical Turk bidding.

questions.question: Which AWS service can be used to automatically scale an application up and down without making capacity planning decisions?
questions.explanation: AWS Auto Scaling automatically scales an application up and down based on demand without manual capacity planning. Redshift, CloudTrail, and Lambda do not serve this auto-scaling role for an application's instances.

questions.question: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) offers which of the following benefits over traditional database management?

options.text: AWS manages the data stored in Amazon RDS tables.
AWS manages the maintenance of the operating system.
AWS automatically scales up instance types on demand.

questions.explanation: With Amazon RDS, AWS manages maintenance of the operating system (patching, etc.), unlike traditional self-managed databases. AWS does not manage your table data, auto-change instance types, or pick your database engine.

questions.question: A company’s web application currently has light dependencies on underlying components so when one component fails the entire web application fails. Applying which AWS Cloud design principle will address the current design issue?

options.text: Implementing elasticity enabling the application to scale up or scale down as demand changes.
Enabling several EC2 instances to run in parallel to achieve better performance.
Focusing on decoupling components by isolating them and ensuring individual components can function when other components.
Doubling EC2 computing resources to increase system fault tolerance.

questions.explanation: The application's tight dependencies (one failure brings down everything) are addressed by decoupling components so each can function independently. Elasticity, parallel instances, and doubling resources do not fix the coupling problem.

questions.question: A customer would like to design and build a new workload on AWS Cloud but does not have the AWS-related software technical expertise in-house. Which of the following AWS programs can a customer take advantage of to achieve that outcome?
questions.explanation: AWS Partner Network (APN) Consulting Partners provide the AWS technical expertise to design and build a workload when a customer lacks it in-house. Technology Partners provide software, Marketplace sells software, and Service Catalog governs products.

questions.question: Which service stores objects, provides real-time access to those objects, and offers versioning and lifecycle capabilities?
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 stores objects with real-time access and offers versioning and lifecycle policies. Glacier is archival, Storage Gateway is hybrid, and EBS is block storage.

questions.question: Distributing workloads across multiple Availability Zones supports which cloud architecture design principle?
questions.explanation: Distributing workloads across multiple Availability Zones supports the 'design for failure' principle, so the loss of one AZ does not take down the application. It is not primarily about automation, agility, or elasticity.

questions.question: Which service should a customer use to consolidate and centrally manage multiple AWS accounts?
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations lets a customer consolidate and centrally manage multiple AWS accounts (with consolidated billing and SCPs). IAM manages identities, SCT converts schemas, and Config tracks configuration.
